question: What is the main reason we use the ABCDEF protocol in emergency care?

options.A: To document nursing care for legal cover
options.B: To figure out the final medical diagnosis
options.C: To replace the need for lab tests
options.D: To find and treat life-threatening problems step-by-step

explanation: You've got this! The ABCDEF guide helps healthcare teams tackle the scariest, most immediate life threats first so nothing gets missed. Great job thinking like an emergency nurse! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T4#GNS315_U3_T4_h1)

question: If a patient is stable and suddenly starts getting worse during an ABCDEF check, what should the team do right away?

options.A: Rush the patient to the operating theatre
options.B: Go straight back to step A and check the airway again
options.C: Finish the rest of the protocol steps first
options.D: Wait at the bedside for the doctor to arrive

explanation: Spot on! If a patient takes a turn for the worse, always cycle right back to the beginning (Airway) to catch any new breathing or airway trouble. Excellent clinical thinking! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T4#GNS315_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why is checking the airway always the very first step in emergency care?

options.A: Hospital rules strictly say airway first
options.B: It keeps the patient from talking too much
options.C: A blocked airway can cause death in minutes
options.D: It is the easiest thing to do in a busy ward

explanation: Spot on! Without a clear airway, oxygen can't reach the lungs, leading to brain death and cardiac arrest very fast. Airway always comes first! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T4#GNS315_U3_T4_h2)

question: An unconscious accident victim is brought in with heavy bleeding in their mouth. What is your very first nursing action?

options.A: Lay them flat on their back without neck support
options.B: Suction the airway while keeping the neck safely supported
options.C: Give oral pain meds to keep them calm
options.D: Send them straight for a chest X-ray

explanation: Brilliant! Clearing the mouth clears the airway, but always remember to protect that vulnerable neck from spinal injury at the same time. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T4#GNS315_U3_T4_h2)

question: What is a major sign that a patient is struggling to breathe during an emergency check?

options.B: Warm, dry skin with pink nail beds
options.C: A steady pulse of 72 beats per minute
options.D: Working hard to breathe and low oxygen saturation

explanation: You nailed it! When a patient is visibly struggling for breath and their oxygen levels drop, it's a clear warning sign that their breathing needs urgent help. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T4#GNS315_U3_T4_h3)

question: Why must a nurse pull back the clothes and actually look at the patient's bare chest during a breathing assessment?

options.A: To listen for tummy sounds in the chest
options.B: To check the exact skin temperature
options.C: To check for chest symmetry, injuries, and odd movements
options.D: To get the skin ready for ECG stickers

explanation: Exactly! Looking closely helps you spot uneven chest rise, hidden wounds, or flail segments that make breathing difficult. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T4#GNS315_U3_T4_h3)

question: What is the fastest, most effective way to stop severe bleeding on a patient's arm or leg?

options.A: Give them water to drink to replace lost blood
options.C: Apply direct pressure or a tourniquet
options.D: Apply ice packs directly to the wound

explanation: Well done! Direct pressure or a tourniquet squeezes those bleeding vessels shut and stops dangerous blood loss fast. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T4#GNS315_U3_T4_h4)

question: A patient in the ER has a fast heart rate, cool sweaty skin, and slow capillary refill. What do these signs tell you?

options.A: They are simply recovering from light exercise
options.B: The brain and heart are getting plenty of oxygen
options.C: Poor blood flow and possible shock
options.D: The nervous system is just overactive

explanation: Spot on! The body pulls blood away from the skin to protect vital organs like the heart and brain when blood volume is low. Classic signs of shock! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T4#GNS315_U3_T4_h4)

question: In the quick AVPU neurological check scale, what does the letter 'V' stand for?
explanation: You got it! V stands for verbal—meaning the patient reacts or speaks when you talk to them. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T4#GNS315_U3_T4_h5)

question: An ER patient is confused, pale, and sleepy. You check their blood sugar and find it is very low at 2.2 mmol/L. What is likely going on?

options.A: The confusion and sleepiness are likely caused by low blood sugar
options.B: They need emergency brain surgery right away
options.C: Their mental state is completely normal for their age
options.D: They have a permanent spinal cord injury

explanation: Brilliant! The brain runs on glucose. When sugar drops too low, confusion sets in—and it usually clears up quickly once sugar is given. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T4#GNS315_U3_T4_h5)

question: What is a major danger when you completely strip off a trauma patient's clothing during the 'Exposure' step?

options.A: Sudden spikes in high blood pressure
options.C: Bad allergic reactions to hospital sheets
options.D: Hypothermia and rapid body heat loss

explanation: Spot on! Cold ER rooms can drop a patient's core temperature fast, and cold blood doesn't clot properly. Always protect their warmth! [learn more](GNS315_U3_T4#GNS315_U3_T4_h6)

question: How should a nurse balance checking a patient's naked skin for injuries while keeping them warm during step 'E'?

options.A: Avoid taking off any clothes at all to keep them warm
options.B: Turn off all room fans to heat up the room
options.C: Leave the patient completely naked for hours to watch their skin
options.D: Uncover body parts briefly to check them, then cover the patient with warm blankets

explanation: You got it! Quick, targeted checks followed by covering them right back up lets you spot injuries without freezing the patient. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T4#GNS315_U3_T4_h6)

question: Aside from taking baseline vital signs, what modern addition does the letter 'F' often stand for in emergency protocols?
explanation: Excellent! Modern emergency care recognizes that having loved ones nearby helps reduce anxiety and supports the patient through a crisis. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T4#GNS315_U3_T4_h7)

question: What is the main job of the support nurse when family members are allowed in the room during an active emergency resuscitation?

options.A: To write down every single drug given by the doctor
options.B: To chase all visitors out of the hospital building
options.C: To do chest compressions if the main rescuer gets tired
options.D: To explain procedures, offer comfort, and answer the family's questions

explanation: Spot on! Having a dedicated nurse look after the family keeps them informed and calm, leaving the rest of the team free to focus fully on saving the patient. [learn more](GNS315_U3_T4#GNS315_U3_T4_h7)
